clue.text: Hands get together to produce this

definitions.text: Hands get together to produce this

parts.words: Hands get together to produce this
parts.note: the clapping of palms together by an audience is what makes the sound of approval being described

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' looks like workers joining forces, but it is the literal palms of an audience coming together.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping is the noise made when people strike their palms together in approval.

clue.text: I'm terrified some scallywag has transgressed

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified that a rascal has broken the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aghast is being struck with horror, as one is when terrified.

clue.text: Shepherd's gone round to the right

parts.note: gone means over, past
a round shape is the letter O
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sheepdog handler has gone round, keeping to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shepherd' here is a minister who tends a flock of people; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a spiritual shepherd tending a congregation, his flock.

clue.text: Water puts a stop to pigs

parts.note: a dam is a barrier that stops a flow
swine are pigs

explanation.surface: Water halts a herd of pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts' is a link word. The answer is a jocular name for water, the only drink Adam had in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous old name for plain drinking water, as the first man had nothing else to drink.

clue.text: Dog needing a pass

definitions.meaning: the Great ... is a mountain pass between Switzerland and Italy

explanation.walkthrough: The dogs were bred by monks at the hospice on the Alpine pass of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A big Swiss rescue breed, and the high Alpine route between Switzerland and Italy named after the same saint.

clue.text: Companion undid corset

indicators.note: undoing the laces of the garment loosens its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's partner unlaced a tight undergarment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undid' rearranges CORSET into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a person who accompanies another, a partner for an outing.

clue.text: Make an impression — with your feet?

definitions.meaning: to press a mark or seal into something
to bring one's foot down hard

explanation.definitionFit: To press a mark into paper with a die, and to thump the ground with a foot.

clue.text: Relation moving from the east

indicators.note: moving the letters about places them in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A family member relocates from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges RELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means belonging to or coming from Asia, the lands where the sun rises.

clue.text: Not disagreeing with a friend in the ring

indicators.note: in puts the friend inside the sound of the ring

parts.note: a ting is the ringing sound of a bell
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A boxer agrees with a pal who is in the boxing ring with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. 'the ring' looks like a boxing ring but is the sound TING.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts that tally correspond, so they are in agreement.

clue.text: Man's fear of Iberia

parts.note: a man's things are his
panic is sudden overwhelming fear

explanation.surface: A man is afraid of Spain and Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hispanic describes things belonging to Spain, the largest country of the peninsula, and by extension Iberia.

clue.text: Deronda unaffected by pride

definitions.meaning: ... Deronda is the title hero of George Eliot's last novel
the biblical prophet thrown into the den was unharmed by the pride of lions there

explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' looks like vanity; it is a group of lions, as in the Book of Daniel.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of Eliot's hero, and the prophet who survived the lions' den unhurt.

clue.text: Cereal I fling about over savoury

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

indicators.note: about places the fling around the word for over

parts.note: to shy is to fling or throw
over means finished, past

explanation.surface: Someone tosses breakfast cereal around a savoury dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SHY around PAST, giving SH-PAST-Y. A Cornish pasty is a meat-and-vegetable pastry from Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry turnover filled with meat and vegetables is a savoury, a non-sweet dish.

clue.text: Caledonian taxes

definitions.meaning: Caledonia is the old Latin name for Scotland, so Caledonian means from Scotland
scot is an old word for a tax or levy, as in scot-free

explanation.definitionFit: People of Scotland, and the plural of an archaic word for levies (hence scot-free).

clue.text: Readily and cheaply available, but you can't buy one now

definitions.meaning: an idiom for things so common they are worth very little
literally, a pair of items for one old penny is a price no shop charges today

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means common and worthless; taken literally it is a price, a pair for a penny, long gone with inflation.

clue.text: Frequently imagined at an assembly

indicators.note: assembly means putting parts together, so the letters of the three words are built up afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps picturing themselves at a school gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' looks like a meeting but rearranges IMAGINED AT AN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means repeatedly, over and over, i.e. often.

clue.text: Weakened during the spring tides

definitions.meaning: in a poor or depressed state
spring tides have the greatest range, so the ebb falls lowest then

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a poor, depleted state; literally it is when the receding sea is furthest out, as at spring tides.

clue.text: Unconvincing nature of two notes to the head

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
me is another note of the sol-fa scale
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness

explanation.surface: Someone attaches a couple of musical notes to the top of a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. NESS (a headland) appears in Scottish place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Weakness in an excuse or argument, its feebleness, is a figurative sense of being crippled.

clue.text: Courtly behaviour from honourable companion heading off competition

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word for competition is removed

parts.note: rivalry is competition

explanation.surface: An honoured courtier behaves gallantly to see off a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the R of RIVALRY to leave IVALRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The knightly code of gallantry and honour shaped courtly conduct.

clue.text: A fast start

parts.note: not a quick getaway but the first day of a period of fasting in the Christian calendar

explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as quick; it means abstaining from food, the first day of Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent, a forty-day season of fasting, begins on this day.

clue.text: Can mostly dispose of cheap decoration

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: mostly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to sell something is to dispose of it

explanation.surface: Most cans can be thrown out along with the tawdry ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims SELL to SEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittering strips hung at Christmas are showy, inexpensive ornament.

clue.text: 2, perhaps, going round in a circle

indicators.note: going round says the letters are spun into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A number goes round and round in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' rearranges CIRCLE. '2' points to the answer of 2 Down, a minister, as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is the general class of which a parish minister is one example.

clue.text: Tumbling water proved sea rough

indicators.note: a rough sea is churned up, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Falling water showed that the sea was choppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges PROVED SEA. The answer is the old sense: rainwater dripping from the roof's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: In its original sense the word was the rainwater that falls from a roof's overhang.

clue.text: Offshoot that is a particle

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for that is to say
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A small branch that is no more than a speck.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is a cutting or shoot of a plant, or a descendant of a family.

clue.text: The Provost's window?

parts.note: the head of one Oxford college is titled Provost, and the college shares its name with a kind of projecting bay window

explanation.walkthrough: The Provost is the head of an Oxford college whose name is also that of an upper-storey bay window.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay window jutting from an upper floor, and the name of the Oxford college headed by a Provost.

clue.text: Hide after returning this French patisserie

indicators.note: after places the hiding place behind the turned French word
returning means the French word is turned back to front

parts.note: ce is French for this
a hide or lair is an animal's hiding place

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a French cake after coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns CE into EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux pastry finger filled with cream is a classic item from a French pastry shop.

clue.text: Jenny, love, the king is the one who decides

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey, jokingly an ass-ess, as a lioness is a female lion
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A list of names: a donkey, a sweetheart and a monarch, with one in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter coins a feminine of ass, like lioness or tigress, for the female donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor is one who evaluates and judges, as a tax or insurance valuer or a tribunal adviser.

clue.text: Gnome giving a talk

definitions.meaning: a gnome is a pithy maxim or aphorism, not a garden figure

explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is an old word for a maxim or proverb, and to be uttering words is to be speaking.

clue.text: Representing an instrument I see and you hear

indicators.note: what you hear is a spoken version, so the sounds of the words before stand for the answer

parts.note: a cymbal is a percussion instrument; I is I and see is said like the letter C

explanation.surface: Someone describes a musical instrument they can see and you can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you hear' turns CYMBAL + I + C into the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something symbolic stands for or signifies something else.
